items.title: Insurers Are Defying Federal Law on Surprise Billing - RealClearHealth
items.reason: The item addresses enforcement and compliance issues with the No Surprises Act, directly relevant to litigation and implementation challenges, though the excerpt alone lacks specific rule changes, case names, or concrete details needed for full revenue-cycle impact assessment.
items.summary: RealClearHealth reports that insurers are not complying with federal No Surprises Act requirements on surprise billing protections. The article indicates systematic defiance of the law by insurers, suggesting enforcement gaps or violations of balance-billing rules established under the Act. This is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as insurer non-compliance affects claim denials, payment disputes, and the Independent Dispute Resolution process that depends on good-faith adherence to surprise billing prohibitions. The piece points to potential litigation or regulatory action that may reshape how insurers handle out-of-network claims and consumer protections.
